features.name: polysyllabic_share_unique_counter_vocab
features.definition: What proportion of the distinct words used across the counter-argument comments are polysyllabic (three or more syllables)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings; malformed/missing input -> null. Concatenate all comments. Lowercase and tokenize with re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", text) (URLs removed first via re.sub(r'https?://\S+','',text)). Take the set of unique word types. Count syllables per word with a fixed heuristic: count groups of consecutive vowels [aeiouy] in the word, subtract 1 if the word ends in a silent 'e' (ends with 'e' but not 'le' preceded by consonant) and count>1; minimum 1. A word is polysyllabic if syllables >= 3. Value = (number of unique polysyllabic types) / (number of unique types). Valid empty list or no words -> null. Pure mechanical computation on raw text; no semantic filtering.

h0: There is no association between polysyllabic_share_unique_counter_vocab and the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Higher polysyllabic_share_unique_counter_vocab is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
note: Operational assumptions: "more polysyllabic words in unique vocabulary" is measured as the share of distinct word types with >=3 syllables, pooled over all counter-comments in OC_comments (other users, not OP). Syllables are a heuristic estimate, not a dictionary count. Persuasiveness is operationalized by the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Raw text may contain quoted text, URLs (removed), or outcome/delta announcements; not filtered. Pooled vocabulary size depends on number/length of comments, which may confound the share; no controls added. List order carries no meaning; reply timing unknown.
